answer: Proof of Useful Work requires agents to solve cryptographic puzzles to join the network. By forcing nodes to commit computational power, similar to how water erodes a karst landscape to reveal deep cedar roots, the system demands real-world energy expenditures. An attacker faces the cost of expensive quartz-based hardware to generate enough hash rate to maintain multiple identities. This economic friction prevents the proliferation of Sybil nodes, ensuring that identity is tethered to verifiable, scarce resource consumption.
